sanskrit: tayos tadā sāditayo raṇāgre mumoha sainyaṃ hariyūthapānām sugrīvanīlāṅgadajāmbavanto na cāpi kiṃ cit pratipedire te
english: When those two were struck down at the forefront of battle, the army of the monkey-chieftains fell into confusion; Sugrīva, Nīla, Aṅgada, and Jāmbavān — none of them could act in any way.

sanskrit: tato viṣaṇṇaṃ samavekṣya sainyaṃ vibhīṣaṇo buddhimatāṃ variṣṭhaḥ uvāca śākhāmṛgarājavīrān āśvāsayann apratimair vacobhiḥ
english: Then Vibhīṣaṇa, foremost among the wise, seeing the army in despair, spoke to the heroic monkey-chieftains, comforting them with incomparable words.

sanskrit: mā bhaiṣṭa nāsty atra viṣādakālo yad āryaputrāv avaśau viṣaṇṇau svayambhuvo vākyam athodvahantau yat sāditāv indrajidastrajālaiḥ
english: "Do not be afraid; this is not a time for despair even though the two noble princes lie helpless and afflicted — it is because they are honoring the word of the Self-Born One that they have been struck down by Indrajit's web of weapons."

sanskrit: tasmai tu dattaṃ paramāstram etat svayambhuvā brāhmam amoghavegam tan mānayantau yadi rājaputrau nipātitau ko 'tra viṣādakālaḥ
english: "This supreme Brahmā weapon of unfailing force was granted by the Self-Born; if the two princes have been laid low while honoring it, what cause is there for despair here?"

sanskrit: brāhmam astraṃ tadā dhīmān mānayitvā tu mārutiḥ vibhīṣaṇavacaḥ śrutvā hanūmāṃs tam athābravīt
english: Then the wise Māruti, having honored the Brahmā weapon, and having heard the words of Vibhīṣaṇa, spoke to him.

sanskrit: etasmin nihate sainye vānarāṇāṃ tarasvinām yo yo dhārayate prāṇāṃs taṃ tam āśvāsayāvahe
english: "Now that this army of swift monkeys has been struck down, let us go and reassure each one who still holds to life."

sanskrit: tāv ubhau yugapad vīrau hanūmad rākṣasottamau ulkāhastau tadā rātrau raṇaśīrṣe viceratuḥ
english: Then those two heroes together, Hanūmān and the foremost of rākṣasas, bearing torches, roamed over the front of the battlefield that night.

sanskrit: chinnalāṅgūlahastorupādāṅguli śiro dharaiḥ sravadbhiḥ kṣatajaṃ gātraiḥ prasravadbhiḥ samantataḥ
english: Strewn all about lay bodies with severed tails, hands, thighs, feet, fingers, and heads, with limbs streaming blood, dripping on every side —

sanskrit: patitaiḥ parvatākārair vānarair abhisaṃkulām śastraiś ca patitair dīptair dadṛśāte vasuṃdharām
english: — they beheld the earth crowded with fallen monkeys huge as mountains and with fallen blazing weapons.

sanskrit: sugrīvam aṅgadaṃ nīlaṃ śarabhaṃ gandhamādanam jāmbavantaṃ suṣeṇaṃ ca vegadarśanam āhukam
english: Sugrīva, Aṅgada, Nīla, Śarabha, Gandhamādana, Jāmbavān, Suṣeṇa, Vegadarśī, and Āhuka —

sanskrit: maindaṃ nalaṃ jyotimukhaṃ dvividaṃ panasaṃ tathā vibhīṣaṇo hanūmāṃś ca dadṛśāte hatān raṇe
english: — Mainda, Nala, Jyotimukha, Dvivida, Panasa, and the rest — Vibhīṣaṇa and Hanūmān saw them lying struck down in battle.

sanskrit: saptaṣaṣṭir hatāḥ koṭyo vānarāṇāṃ tarasvinām ahnaḥ pañcamaśeṣeṇa vallabhena svayambhuvaḥ
english: Sixty-seven crores of swift monkeys had been slain within the remaining fifth part of the day by the weapon dear to the Self-Born.

sanskrit: sāgaraughanibhaṃ bhīmaṃ dṛṣṭvā bāṇārditaṃ balam mārgate jāmbavantaṃ sma hanūmān savibhīṣaṇaḥ
english: Seeing that dreadful army, vast as an ocean flood, tormented by arrows, Hanūmān together with Vibhīṣaṇa searched for Jāmbavān.

sanskrit: svabhāvajarayā yuktaṃ vṛddhaṃ śaraśataiś citam prajāpatisutaṃ vīraṃ śāmyantam iva pāvakam
english: They found the aged one, afflicted by natural old age, pierced by hundreds of arrows, the heroic son of Prajāpati, like a fire dying down.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā tam upasaṃgamya paulastyo vākyam abravīt kaccid āryaśarais tīrṣṇair na prāṇā dhvaṃsitās tava
english: Seeing him, the descendant of Pulastya approached and spoke: "O noble one, have your vital breaths not been destroyed by these sharp arrows?"

sanskrit: vibhīṣaṇavacaḥ śrutvā jāmbavān ṛkṣapuṃgavaḥ kṛcchrād abhyudgiran vākyam idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: Hearing Vibhīṣaṇa's words, Jāmbavān, the foremost of bears, with great difficulty drew out a breath and spoke these words:

sanskrit: nairṛtendramahāvīryasvareṇa tvābhilakṣaye pīḍyamānaḥ śitair bāṇair na tvāṃ paśyāmi cakṣuṣā
english: "By your voice — the voice of a great hero, lord of rākṣasas — I recognize you; tormented as I am by sharp arrows, I cannot see you with my eyes."

sanskrit: añjanā suprajā yena mātariśvā ca nairṛta hanūmān vānaraśreṣṭhaḥ prāṇān dhārayate kva cit
english: "Tell me, O lord of rākṣasas — is Añjanā's noble son, through whom Mātariśvan lives again, that best of monkeys, Hanūmān, alive somewhere?"

sanskrit: śrutvā jāmbavato vākyam uvācedaṃ vibhīṣaṇaḥ āryaputrāv atikramya kasmāt pṛcchasi mārutim
english: Hearing Jāmbavān's words, Vibhīṣaṇa said: "Passing over the two noble princes, why do you ask after the son of the Wind?"

sanskrit: naiva rājani sugrīve nāṅgade nāpi rāghave ārya saṃdarśitaḥ sneho yathā vāyusute paraḥ
english: "Not toward king Sugrīva, not toward Aṅgada, not even toward Rāghava, O noble one, is love displayed as greatly as toward the son of the Wind."

sanskrit: vibhīṣaṇavacaḥ śrutvā jāmbavān vākyam abravīt śṛṇu nairṛtaśārdūla yasmāt pṛcchāmi mārutim
english: Hearing Vibhīṣaṇa's words, Jāmbavān replied: "Hear, O tiger among rākṣasas, why I ask after Māruti —"

sanskrit: tasmiñ jīvati vīre tu hatam apy ahataṃ balam hanūmaty ujjhitaprāṇe jīvanto 'pi vayaṃ hatāḥ
english: "While that hero lives, even an army slain is as if unslain; but if Hanūmān has abandoned his life, then though we live, we are as the dead."

sanskrit: dhriyate mārutis tāta mārutapratimo yadi vaiśvānarasamo vīrye jīvitāśā tato bhavet
english: "If Māruti, who is like the Wind itself, equal to fire in valor, still lives, dear friend, then there is hope of life."

sanskrit: tato vṛddham upāgamya niyamenābhyavādayat gṛhya jāmbavataḥ pādau hanūmān mārutātmajaḥ
english: Then the son of the Wind, Hanūmān, came to the aged one and paid him due reverence, grasping the feet of Jāmbavān.

sanskrit: śrutvā hanumato vākyaṃ tathāpi vyathitendriyaḥ punarjātam ivātmānaṃ sa mene ṛkṣapuṃgavaḥ
english: Hearing Hanūmān's voice, though his senses were afflicted, the foremost of bears felt himself reborn as it were.

sanskrit: tato 'bravīn mahātejā hanūmantaṃ sa jāmbavān āgaccha hariśārdūlavānarāṃs trātum arhasi
english: Then the greatly resplendent Jāmbavān said to Hanūmān: "Come, O tiger among monkeys — you must save the vānaras."

sanskrit: nānyo vikramaparyāptas tvam eṣāṃ paramaḥ sakhā tvatparākramakālo 'yaṃ nānyaṃ paśyāmi kañ cana
english: "No other is equal to the task in prowess; you are their supreme protector. This is the moment for your valor — I see no one else."

sanskrit: ṛkṣavānaravīrāṇām anīkāni praharṣaya viśalyau kuru cāpy etau sāditau rāmalakṣmaṇau
english: "Gladden the troops of bear and monkey heroes; and remove the arrows from these two who have been struck — Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa."

sanskrit: gatvā paramam adhvānam upary upari sāgaram himavantaṃ nagaśreṣṭhaṃ hanūman gantum arhasi
english: "Travelling a great distance, high above the ocean, O Hanūmān, you must go to the Himālaya, the foremost of mountains."

sanskrit: tataḥ kāñcanam atyugram ṛṣabhaṃ parvatottamam kailāsaśikharaṃ cāpi drakṣyasy ariniṣūdana
english: "Then, O destroyer of foes, you will see the supremely towering golden Ṛṣabha mountain, and also the peak of Kailāsa."

sanskrit: tayoḥ śikharayor madhye pradīptam atulaprabham sarvauṣadhiyutaṃ vīra drakṣyasy auṣadhiparvatam
english: "Between those two peaks, blazing with incomparable splendor, O hero, you will see the Herb Mountain, replete with all medicinal plants."

sanskrit: tasya vānaraśārdūlacatasro mūrdhni saṃbhavāḥ drakṣyasy oṣadhayo dīptā dīpayantyo diśo daśa
english: "O tiger among monkeys, on its summit you will see four blazing herbs that illuminate all ten directions."

sanskrit: mṛtasaṃjīvanīṃ caiva viśalyakaraṇīm api sauvarṇakaraṇīṃ caiva saṃdhānīṃ ca mahauṣadhīm
english: "There is Mṛtasaṃjīvanī that revives the dead, Viśalyakaraṇī that removes arrows, Sauvarṇakaraṇī that restores golden color, and Saṃdhānī the great healing herb."

sanskrit: tāḥ sarvā hanuman gṛhya kṣipram āgantum arhasi āśvāsaya harīn prāṇair yojya gandhavahātmajaḥ
english: "Gathering all of them, you must come quickly, O Hanūmān, son of the Wind-god; reuniting the monkeys with their lives, revive them."

sanskrit: śrutvā jāmbavato vākyaṃ hanūmān haripuṃgavaḥ āpūryata baloddharṣais toyavegair ivārṇavaḥ
english: Hearing Jāmbavān's words, Hanūmān, the bull among monkeys, swelled with an upsurge of strength like an ocean swelling with rushing waters.

sanskrit: sa parvatataṭāgrasthaḥ pīḍayan parvatottaram hanūmān dṛśyate vīro dvitīya iva parvataḥ
english: Standing at the mountain's edge and pressing down upon that great mountain, the hero Hanūmān appeared himself like a second mountain.

sanskrit: haripādavinirbhinno niṣasāda sa parvataḥ na śaśāka tadātmānaṃ soḍhuṃ bhṛśanipīḍitaḥ
english: That mountain, shattered by the monkey's feet, sank down; it could not withstand itself under such tremendous pressure.

sanskrit: tasya petur nagā bhūmau harivegāc ca jajvaluḥ śṛṅgāṇi ca vyakīryanta pīḍitasya hanūmatā
english: The trees fell to the ground and burst into flame from the monkey's force; its peaks were scattered as Hanūmān pressed upon it.

sanskrit: tasmin saṃpīḍyamāne tu bhagnadrumaśilātale na śekur vānarāḥ sthātuṃ ghūrṇamāne nagottame
english: As the great mountain was being pressed down, its floor of trees and rocks shattered, the monkeys could not stand upon it as it whirled about.

sanskrit: sa ghūrṇitamahādvārā prabhagnagṛhagopurā laṅkā trāsākulā rātrau pranṛttevābhavat tadā
english: Laṅkā with its great gates whirling, its houses and gateways shattered, filled with terror in the night, seemed as though it were dancing.

sanskrit: pṛthivīdharasaṃkāśo nipīḍya dharaṇīdharam pṛthivīṃ kṣobhayām āsa sārṇavāṃ mārutātmajaḥ
english: Resembling a mountain himself, the son of Māruta, pressing down on the mountain-bearer, caused the earth together with its oceans to shake.

sanskrit: padbhyāṃ tu śailam āpīḍya vaḍavāmukhavan mukham vivṛtyograṃ nanādoccais trāsayann iva rākṣasān
english: Pressing upon the mountain with his feet and opening his terrible mouth like the submarine fire, he roared mightily as if to terrify the rākṣasas.

sanskrit: tasya nānadyamānasya śrutvā ninadam adbhutam laṅkāsthā rākṣasāḥ sarve na śekuḥ spandituṃ bhayāt
english: Hearing that wondrous roar as he bellowed, all the rākṣasas dwelling in Laṅkā could not stir from fear.

sanskrit: namaskṛtvātha rāmāya mārutir bhīmavikramaḥ rāghavārthe paraṃ karma samaihata paraṃtapaḥ
english: Then Māruti of terrible might, the scorcher of foes, having paid homage to Rāma, set himself to the supreme task for Rāghava's sake.

sanskrit: sa puccham udyamya bhujaṃgakalpaṃ vinamya pṛṣṭhaṃ śravaṇe nikuñcya vivṛtya vaktraṃ vaḍavāmukhābham āpupluve vyomni sa caṇḍavegaḥ
english: Raising his tail like a great serpent, bending his back, contracting his ears, opening his mouth like the submarine fire, he of fierce speed leaped into the sky.

sanskrit: sa vṛkṣaṣaṇḍāṃs tarasā jahāra śailāñ śilāḥ prākṛtavānarāṃś ca bāhūruvegoddhatasaṃpraṇunnās te kṣīṇavegāḥ salile nipetuḥ
english: He swiftly swept away groves of trees, mountains, and rocks; and ordinary monkeys, struck and sent flying by the force of his arms and thighs, fell spent into the water.

sanskrit: sa tau prasāryoragabhogakalpau bhujau bhujaṃgārinikāśavīryaḥ jagāma meruṃ nagarājam agryaṃ diśaḥ prakarṣann iva vāyusūnuḥ
english: Stretching out his two arms like the coils of a great serpent, valiant as the enemy of serpents, the son of the Wind went toward Meru, king of mountains, seemingly drawing the directions behind him.

sanskrit: sa sāgaraṃ ghūrṇitavīcimālaṃ tadā bhṛśaṃ bhrāmitasarvasattvam samīkṣamāṇaḥ sahasā jagāma cakraṃ yathā viṣṇukarāgramuktam
english: Gazing upon the ocean with its tossing rows of waves, its every creature thrown into agitation, he went suddenly like the discus released from the tip of Viṣṇu's hand.

sanskrit: sa parvatān vṛkṣagaṇān sarāṃsi nadīs taṭākāni purottamāni sphītāñjanāṃs tān api saṃprapaśyañ jagāma vegāt pitṛtulyavegaḥ
english: Beholding mountains, forests, lakes, rivers, reservoirs, the finest cities, and even prosperous tracts of collyrium, he sped onward with speed equal to his father's.

sanskrit: ādityapatham āśritya jagāma sa gataśramaḥ sa dadarśa hariśreṣṭho himavantaṃ nagottamam
english: Taking the path of the sun, he went without fatigue; that foremost of monkeys beheld the Himālaya, highest of mountains.

sanskrit: nānāprasravaṇopetaṃ bahukaṃdaranirjharam śvetābhracayasaṃkāśaiḥ śikharaiś cārudarśanaiḥ
english: It was adorned with many springs, filled with numerous gorges and cascades, with peaks resembling heaps of white clouds and fair to behold.

sanskrit: sa taṃ samāsādya mahānagendram atipravṛddhottamaghoraśṛṅgam dadarśa puṇyāni mahāśramāṇi surarṣisaṃghottamasevitāni
english: Approaching that lord of great mountains with its very lofty, foremost, and terrible peaks, he saw the holy great hermitages frequented by the foremost hosts of gods and seers.

sanskrit: sa brahmakośaṃ rajatālayaṃ ca śakrālayaṃ rudraśarapramokṣam hayānanaṃ brahmaśiraś ca dīptaṃ dadarśa vaivasvata kiṃkarāṃś ca
english: He saw Brahmā's treasury, the Silver Abode, Indra's dwelling, the spot where Rudra released his arrow, the horse-faced Hayaśīrṣa, the blazing Brahmaśiras, and the attendants of Vaivasvata Yama.

sanskrit: vajrālayaṃ vaiśvaraṇālayaṃ ca sūryaprabhaṃ sūryanibandhanaṃ ca brahmāsanaṃ śaṃkarakārmukaṃ ca dadarśa nābhiṃ ca vasuṃdharāyāḥ
english: He saw the abode of Vajra, the dwelling of Vaiśravaṇa bright as the sun, the tethering place of the sun, the seat of Brahmā, the bow of Śaṃkara, and the navel of the earth.

sanskrit: kailāsam agryaṃ himavacchilāṃ ca tatharṣabhaṃ kāñcanaśailam agryam sa dīptasarvauṣadhisaṃpradīptaṃ dadarśa sarvauṣadhiparvatendram
english: He saw the foremost Kailāsa, the Himālayan rock, the Ṛṣabha mountain foremost of golden peaks, blazing with every herb ablaze, the king of the Herb Mountain.

sanskrit: sa taṃ samīkṣyānalaraśmidīptaṃ visiṣmiye vāsavadūtasūnuḥ āplutya taṃ cauṣadhiparvatendraṃ tatrauṣadhīnāṃ vicayaṃ cakāra
english: Beholding it blazing with rays like fire, the son of Indra's messenger was filled with wonder; leaping upon that king of herb mountains, he set about gathering the herbs there.

sanskrit: sa yojanasahasrāṇi samatītya mahākapiḥ divyauṣadhidharaṃ śailaṃ vyacaran mārutātmajaḥ
english: That great monkey, the son of Māruta, having crossed thousands of yojanas, roamed over the mountain bearing divine herbs.

sanskrit: mahauṣadhyas tu tāḥ sarvās tasmin parvatasattame vijñāyārthinam āyāntaṃ tato jagmur adarśanam
english: But all those great herbs on that best of mountains, knowing that a seeker was approaching, then became invisible.

sanskrit: sa tā mahātmā hanumān apaśyaṃś cukopa kopāc ca bhṛśaṃ nanāda amṛṣyamāṇo 'gninikāśacakṣur mahīdharendraṃ tam uvāca vākyam
english: The great-souled Hanūmān, not seeing them, became enraged; seething with anger, he roared mightily; with eyes blazing like fire, unable to endure it, he spoke to that lord of mountains:

sanskrit: kim etad evaṃ suviniścitaṃ te yad rāghave nāsi kṛtānukampaḥ paśyādya madbāhubalābhibhūto vikīrṇam ātmānam atho nagendra
english: "What is this that you have so firmly resolved — that you show no compassion for Rāghava? Behold yourself now scattered asunder, overcome by the strength of my arms, O lord of mountains!"

sanskrit: sa tasya śṛṅgaṃ sanagaṃ sanāgaṃ sakāñcanaṃ dhātusahasrajuṣṭam vikīrṇakūṭaṃ calitāgrasānuṃ pragṛhya vegāt sahasonmamātha
english: Seizing at once with speed its peak with all its trees, elephants, gold, and thousands of minerals — its summit scattered, its upper ridges shaking — he uprooted it.

sanskrit: sa taṃ samutpāṭya kham utpapāta vitrāsya lokān sasurān surendrān saṃstūyamānaḥ khacarair anekair jagāma vegād garuḍogravīryaḥ
english: Having uprooted it, he leaped into the sky, terrifying the worlds along with the gods and lords of gods; praised by many sky-dwellers, he went with the fierce power of Garuḍa.

sanskrit: sa bhāskarādhvānam anuprapannas tad bhāskarābhaṃ śikharaṃ pragṛhya babhau tadā bhāskarasaṃnikāśo raveḥ samīpe pratibhāskarābhaḥ
english: Entering the path of the sun, holding that peak bright as the sun, he shone then, himself like the sun, near the sun, reflecting back the sun's brightness.

sanskrit: sa tena śailena bhṛśaṃ rarāja śailopamo gandhavahātmajas tu sahasradhāreṇa sapāvakena cakreṇa khe viṣṇur ivoddhṛtena
english: The son of the Wind-god, like a mountain himself, shone magnificently with that mountain, like Viṣṇu in the sky holding aloft his discus with its thousand edges blazing with fire.

sanskrit: taṃ vānarāḥ prekṣya tadā vineduḥ sa tān api prekṣya mudā nanāda teṣāṃ samudghuṣṭaravaṃ niśamya laṅkālayā bhīmataraṃ vineduḥ
english: The monkeys, seeing him, cried out; he too, seeing them, roared with joy. Hearing their mingled cries, those dwelling in Laṅkā cried out even more terribly.

sanskrit: tato mahātmā nipapāta tasmiñ śailottame vānarasainyamadhye haryuttamebhyaḥ śirasābhivādya vibhīṣaṇaṃ tatra ca sasvaje saḥ
english: Then the great-souled one descended with that foremost mountain into the midst of the monkey army, bowing his head to the foremost monkeys, and there he embraced Vibhīṣaṇa.

sanskrit: tāv apy ubhau mānuṣarājaputrau taṃ gandham āghrāya mahauṣadhīnām babhūvatus tatra tadā viśalyāv uttasthur anye ca haripravīrāḥ
english: Those two also, the princes born as men, inhaling the fragrance of the great herbs, became free of their arrow-wounds; and other heroic monkeys rose up.

sanskrit: tato harir gandhavahātmajas tu tam oṣadhīśailam udagravīryaḥ nināya vegād dhimavantam eva punaś ca rāmeṇa samājagāma
english: Then Hari, the son of the Wind-god, of exalted valor, swiftly carried that Herb Mountain back to the Himālaya itself, and returned again to Rāma.

sanskrit: tato 'bravīn mahātejāḥ sugrīvo vānarādhipaḥ arthyaṃ vijāpayaṃś cāpi hanūmantaṃ mahābalam
english: Then the greatly resplendent Sugrīva, lord of the monkeys, also communicating his purpose, spoke to the mighty Hanūmān:

sanskrit: yato hataḥ kumbhakarṇaḥ kumārāś ca niṣūditāḥ nedānīm upanirhāraṃ rāvaṇo dātum arhati
english: "Since Kumbhakarṇa has been slain and the princes have been killed, Rāvaṇa is no longer in a position to deliver reinforcements now."

sanskrit: ye ye mahābalāḥ santi laghavaś ca plavaṃgamāḥ laṅkām abhyutpatantv āśu gṛhyolkāḥ plavagarṣabhāḥ
english: "Let all the monkeys who are mighty and swift leap at Laṅkā quickly, O bulls among monkeys, taking up torches."

sanskrit: tato 'staṃ gata āditye raudre tasmin niśāmukhe laṅkām abhimukhāḥ solkā jagmus te plavagarṣabhāḥ
english: Then, when the sun had set at that terrible twilight, those bulls among monkeys, bearing torches, went facing toward Laṅkā.

sanskrit: ulkāhastair harigaṇaiḥ sarvataḥ samabhidrutāḥ ārakṣasthā virūpākṣāḥ sahasā vipradudruvuḥ
english: Charged on all sides by the monkey troops holding torches, the disfigured-eyed guards stationed at the walls suddenly fled in all directions.

sanskrit: gopurāṭṭa pratolīṣu caryāsu vividhāsu ca prāsādeṣu ca saṃhṛṣṭāḥ sasṛjus te hutāśanam
english: Exulting, the monkeys set fire to the gateways, watchtowers, wide avenues, patrol-paths of various kinds, and palaces.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ gṛhasahasrāṇi dadāha hutabhuk tadā āvāsān rākṣasānāṃ ca sarveṣāṃ gṛhamedhinām
english: Then the fire devoured thousands of those houses and the dwellings of all the rākṣasas, of every householder.

sanskrit: hemacitratanutrāṇāṃ sragdāmāmbaradhāriṇām sīdhupānacalākṣāṇāṃ madavihvalagāminām
english: Of those whose armor was adorned with gold, who wore garlands of flowers and fine garments, whose eyes were unsteady with the drinking of wine, who walked reeling with intoxication —

sanskrit: kāntālambitavastrāṇāṃ śatrusaṃjātamanyunām gadāśūlāsi hastānāṃ khādatāṃ pibatām api
english: — whose garments clung to their beloved consorts, who were filled with fury toward their enemies, who held maces, spears, and swords in their hands, who were still eating and drinking —

sanskrit: śayaneṣu mahārheṣu prasuptānāṃ priyaiḥ saha trastānāṃ gacchatāṃ tūrṇaṃ putrān ādāya sarvataḥ
english: — who lay asleep on their fine couches together with their beloved ones, or who fled in terror swiftly, taking their children with them, in all directions —

sanskrit: teṣāṃ gṛhasahasrāṇi tadā laṅkānivāsinām adahat pāvakas tatra jajvāla ca punaḥ punaḥ
english: — the fire burned thousands of those houses of the Laṅkā-dwellers, and blazed again and again.

sanskrit: sāravanti mahārhāṇi gambhīraguṇavanti ca hemacandrārdhacandrāṇi candraśālonnatāni ca
english: The solid, greatly valuable dwellings, possessed of deep merits, adorned with golden full moons and half-moons, with their lofty moonlight chambers —

sanskrit: ratnacitragavākṣāṇi sādhiṣṭhānāni sarvaśaḥ maṇividrumacitrāṇi spṛśantīva ca bhāskaram
english: — with their lattice-windows inlaid with gems, with their bases firm on all sides, painted with jewels and coral, seeming to touch the sun —

sanskrit: krauñcabarhiṇavīṇānāṃ bhūṣaṇānāṃ ca nisvanaiḥ nāditāny acalābhāni veśmāny agnir dadāha saḥ
english: — the mansions that resounded with the sounds of curlews, peacocks, lutes, and ornaments, immovable like mountains — the fire devoured them.

sanskrit: jvalanena parītāni toraṇāni cakāśire vidyudbhir iva naddhāni meghajālāni gharmage
english: The gateways, encircled by fire, shone like masses of clouds bound with lightning in the summer season.

sanskrit: vimāneṣu prasuptāś ca dahyamānā varāṅganāḥ tyaktābharaṇasaṃyogā hāhety uccair vicukruśuḥ
english: Noble women who had been sleeping in the aerial palaces, being burned, shedding their jewelry, cried out loudly: "Alas! Alas!"

sanskrit: tatra cāgniparītāni nipetur bhavanāny api vajrivajrahatānīva śikharāṇi mahāgireḥ
english: There the mansions, enveloped in fire, collapsed, like the peaks of a great mountain struck by Indra's thunderbolt.

sanskrit: tāni nirdahyamānāni dūrataḥ pracakāśire himavacchikharāṇīva dīptauṣadhivanāni ca
english: Those blazing mansions shone from afar like the peaks of the Himālaya with their forests of blazing herbs.

sanskrit: harmyāgrair dahyamānaiś ca jvālāprajvalitair api rātrau sā dṛśyate laṅkā puṣpitair iva kiṃśukaiḥ
english: With the palace-tops burning and blazing with flames, Laṅkā at night appeared as if covered with flowering kiṃśuka trees.

sanskrit: hastyadhyakṣair gajair muktair muktaiś ca turagair api babhūva laṅkā lokānte bhrāntagrāha ivārṇavaḥ
english: With elephants released by their keepers and horses set free, Laṅkā became like an ocean at the end of the world with sharks swimming in disorder.

sanskrit: aśvaṃ muktaṃ gajo dṛṣṭvā kaccid bhīto 'pasarpati bhīto bhītaṃ gajaṃ dṛṣṭvā kva cid aśvo nivartate
english: Seeing a horse set free, an elephant perhaps turns aside in fear; a horse, frightened, seeing a frightened elephant, turns back somewhere.

sanskrit: sā babhūva muhūrtena haribhir dīpitā purī lokasyāsya kṣaye ghore pradīpteva vasuṃdharā
english: That city, set ablaze by the monkeys in a moment, became like the earth blazing at the terrible dissolution of this world.

sanskrit: nārī janasya dhūmena vyāptasyoccair vineduṣaḥ svano jvalanataptasya śuśruve daśayojanam
english: The cries of the women, enveloped in smoke, wailing loudly, the sound of those scorched by fire, were heard for ten yojanas.

sanskrit: pradagdhakāyān aparān rākṣasān nirgatān bahiḥ sahasābhyutpatanti sma harayo 'tha yuyutsavaḥ
english: The monkeys, eager for battle, suddenly leaped upon other rākṣasas whose bodies had been scorched and who had come outside.

sanskrit: udghuṣṭaṃ vānarāṇāṃ ca rākṣasānāṃ ca nisvanaḥ diśo daśa samudraṃ ca pṛthivīṃ cānvanādayat
english: The battle-cries of the monkeys and the shrieks of the rākṣasas resounded through the ten directions, through the ocean, and through the earth.

sanskrit: viśalyau tu mahātmānau tāv ubhau rāmalakṣmaṇau asaṃbhrāntau jagṛhatus tāv ubhau dhanuṣī vare
english: Those two great-souled ones, Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, freed from their arrows, unperturbed, took up their two excellent bows.

sanskrit: tato visphārayāṇasya rāmasya dhanur uttamam babhūva tumulaḥ śabdo rākṣasānāṃ bhayāvahaḥ
english: Then as Rāma twanged his excellent bow, a tumultuous sound arose, causing terror among the rākṣasas.

sanskrit: aśobhata tadā rāmo dhanur visphārayan mahat bhagavān iva saṃkruddho bhavo vedamayaṃ dhanuḥ
english: Then Rāma shone brilliantly, drawing back his great bow, like the blessed and furious Bhava with his bow that is the Veda.

sanskrit: vānarodghuṣṭaghoṣaś ca rākṣasānāṃ ca nisvanaḥ jyāśabdaś cāpi rāmasya trayaṃ vyāpa diśo daśa
english: The terrible cry of the monkeys, the wail of the rākṣasas, and the twang of Rāma's bowstring — these three filled the ten directions.

sanskrit: tasya kārmukamuktaiś ca śarais tatpuragopuram kailāsaśṛṅgapratimaṃ vikīrṇam apatad bhuvi
english: By the arrows released from his bow, the city gate of that fortress, resembling a peak of Kailāsa, was shattered and fell to the earth.

sanskrit: tato rāmaśarān dṛṣṭvā vimāneṣu gṛheṣu ca saṃnāho rākṣasendrāṇāṃ tumulaḥ samapadyata
english: Then seeing Rāma's arrows, tumultuous arming of the rākṣasa lords occurred in the aerial palaces and houses.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ saṃnahyamānānāṃ siṃhanādaṃ ca kurvatām śarvarī rākṣasendrāṇāṃ raudrīva samapadyata
english: As they armed themselves and raised their lion-roars, the night of the rākṣasa lords became as it were dreadful.

sanskrit: ādiṣṭā vānarendrās te sugrīveṇa mahātmanā āsannā dvāram āsādya yudhyadhvaṃ plavagarṣabhāḥ
english: Those lords of monkeys, commanded by the great-souled Sugrīva, having approached close, reaching the gate: "Fight, O bulls among monkeys!"

sanskrit: yaś ca vo vitathaṃ kuryāt tatra tatra vyavasthitaḥ sa hantavyo 'bhisaṃplutya rājaśāsanadūṣakaḥ
english: "And whoever stationed at his post violates his duty — he must be killed outright, as one who violates the king's command."

sanskrit: teṣu vānaramukhyeṣu dīptolkojjvalapāṇiṣu sthiteṣu dvāram āsādya rāvaṇaṃ manyur āviśat
english: As those foremost monkeys stood at the gate with blazing torches flaming in their hands, fury entered Rāvaṇa.

sanskrit: tasya jṛmbhitavikṣepād vyāmiśrā vai diśo daśa rūpavān iva rudrasya manyur gātreṣv adṛśyata
english: From the spreading convulsions of his agitation the ten directions were thrown into confusion; his fury was visible in his limbs as if it had taken the form of Rudra's wrath.

sanskrit: sa nikumbhaṃ ca kumbhaṃ ca kumbhakarṇātmajāv ubhau preṣayām āsa saṃkruddho rākṣasair bahubhiḥ saha
english: Seething with rage, he dispatched Nikumbha and Kumbha, both sons of Kumbhakarṇa, together with many rākṣasas.

sanskrit: śaśāsa caiva tān sarvān rākṣasān rākṣaseśvaraḥ rākṣasā gacchatātraiva siṃhanādaṃ ca nādayan
english: The lord of rākṣasas commanded all those rākṣasas: "Go there at once, rākṣasas!" — and they roared with lion-roars.

sanskrit: tatas tu coditās tena rākṣasā jvalitāyudhāḥ laṅkāyā niryayur vīrāḥ praṇadantaḥ punaḥ punaḥ
english: Then those heroes, spurred on by him, the rākṣasas with their weapons ablaze, issued forth from Laṅkā, roaring again and again.

sanskrit: bhīmāśvarathamātaṃgaṃ nānāpatti samākulam dīptaśūlagadākhaḍgaprāsatomarakārmukam
english: With terrible horses, chariots, and elephants, swarming with infantry of various kinds, armed with blazing spears, maces, swords, javelins, darts, and bows —

sanskrit: tad rākṣasabalaṃ ghoraṃ bhīmavikramapauruṣam dadṛśe jvalitaprāsaṃ kiṅkiṇīśatanāditam
english: — that dreadful rākṣasa army of terrible prowess and valor was seen blazing with javelins, resounding with hundreds of small bells.

sanskrit: hemajālācitabhujaṃ vyāveṣṭitaparaśvadham vyāghūrṇitamahāśastraṃ bāṇasaṃsaktakārmukam
english: Arms latticed with golden networks, battle-axes bound tight, great weapons swung in sweeping arcs, bows pressed together with arrows —

sanskrit: gandhamālyamadhūtsekasaṃmodita mahānilam ghoraṃ śūrajanākīrṇaṃ mahāmbudharanisvanam
english: — with a great wind fragrant with perfumes, garlands, and the effusion of honey, dreadful, swarming with brave men, roaring like a great storm-cloud —

sanskrit: taṃ dṛṣṭvā balam āyāntaṃ rākṣasānāṃ sudāruṇam saṃcacāla plavaṃgānāṃ balam uccair nanāda ca
english: Seeing that very terrible army of the rākṣasas advancing, the monkey army stirred and cried out loudly.

sanskrit: javenāplutya ca punas tad rākṣasabalaṃ mahat abhyayāt pratyaribalaṃ pataṃga iva pāvakam
english: Leaping forward swiftly, the great monkey army charged the enemy force like moths rushing into fire.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ bhujaparāmarśavyāmṛṣṭaparighāśani rākṣasānāṃ balaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ bhūyastaram aśobhata
english: The foremost force of the rākṣasas, with its iron bars and thunderbolts sweeping and striking from the swinging of their arms, shone even more magnificently.

sanskrit: tathaivāpy apare teṣāṃ kapīnām asibhiḥ śitaiḥ pravīrān abhito jaghnur ghorarūpā niśācarāḥ
english: Likewise other night-wanderers of terrible form struck the foremost of those monkeys on every side with sharp swords.

sanskrit: ghnantam anyaṃ jaghānānyaḥ pātayantam apātayat garhamāṇaṃ jagarhānye daśantam apare 'daśat
english: One struck him who was striking another; one felled him who was felling; others reviled the one reviling; others bit the one biting.

sanskrit: dehīty anye dadāty anyo dadāmīty aparaḥ punaḥ kiṃ kleśayasi tiṣṭheti tatrānyonyaṃ babhāṣire
english: "Give it!" some cried; "He's giving it!" another; "I'll give it!" yet another again; "Why do you trouble me? Stand!" — thus they spoke to one another there.

sanskrit: samudyatamahāprāsaṃ muṣṭiśūlāsisaṃkulam prāvartata mahāraudraṃ yuddhaṃ vānararakṣasām
english: With great javelins raised aloft, with fists, spears, and swords in confusion, a mighty and dreadful battle of the monkeys and rākṣasas commenced.

sanskrit: vānarān daśa sapteti rākṣasā abhyapātayan rākṣasān daśasapteti vānarā jaghnur āhave
english: The rākṣasas attacked ten, seventeen monkeys at a time; the monkeys slew ten and seventeen rākṣasas in battle.

sanskrit: visrastakeśarasanaṃ vimuktakavacadhvajam balaṃ rākṣasam ālambya vānarāḥ paryavārayan
english: The monkeys, seizing the rākṣasa army with its manes and harnesses fallen loose, its armor and standards discarded, surrounded it on all sides.

sanskrit: pravṛtte saṃkule tasmin ghore vīrajanakṣaye aṅgadaḥ kampanaṃ vīram āsasāda raṇotsukaḥ
english: As that terrible confused slaughter of heroes raged, the battle-eager Aṅgada encountered the hero Kampana.

sanskrit: āhūya so 'ṅgadaṃ kopāt tāḍayām āsa vegitaḥ gadayā kampanaḥ pūrvaṃ sa cacāla bhṛśāhataḥ
english: Challenging Aṅgada, Kampana in his fury swiftly struck him first with his mace; struck mightily, Aṅgada staggered.

sanskrit: sa saṃjñāṃ prāpya tejasvī cikṣepa śikharaṃ gireḥ arditaś ca prahāreṇa kampanaḥ patito bhuvi
english: Recovering consciousness, the valiant one hurled a mountain peak; and Kampana, tormented by the blow, fell to the earth.

sanskrit: hatapravīrā vyathitā rākṣasendracamūs tadā jagāmābhimukhī sā tu kumbhakarṇasuto yataḥ āpatantīṃ ca vegena kumbhas tāṃ sāntvayac camūm
english: With its heroes slain and afflicted, the rākṣasa king's army then turned toward where the son of Kumbhakarṇa was; as it rushed forward with speed, Kumbha calmed that army.

sanskrit: sa dhanur dhanvināṃ śreṣṭhaḥ pragṛhya susamāhitaḥ mumocāśīviṣaprakhyāñ śarān dehavidāraṇān
english: That best of archers, taking up his bow with perfect composure, released arrows like venomous serpents that tear through bodies.

sanskrit: tasya tac chuśubhe bhūyaḥ saśaraṃ dhanur uttamam vidyudairāvatārciṣmad dvitīyendradhanur yathā
english: His excellent bow with its arrows shone still more brilliantly, like a second Indra's bow blazing with the light of Airāvata's lightning.

sanskrit: ākarṇakṛṣṭamuktena jaghāna dvividaṃ tadā tena hāṭakapuṅkhena patriṇā patravāsasā
english: Released from a full draw to the ear, with that arrow with golden shaft, feathered, clad in feathers, he then struck Dvivida.

sanskrit: sahasābhihatas tena vipramuktapadaḥ sphuran nipapātādrikūṭābho vihvalaḥ plavagottamaḥ
english: Suddenly struck by him, his footing lost, convulsing, bewildered, that foremost of monkeys fell like a mountain peak.

sanskrit: maindas tu bhrātaraṃ dṛṣṭvā bhagnaṃ tatra mahāhave abhidudrāva vegena pragṛhya mahatīṃ śilām
english: But Mainda, seeing his brother broken in that great battle, charged forward swiftly, grasping a great boulder.

sanskrit: tāṃ śilāṃ tu pracikṣepa rākṣasāya mahābalaḥ bibheda tāṃ śilāṃ kumbhaḥ prasannaiḥ pañcabhiḥ śaraiḥ
english: That mighty one hurled the boulder at the rākṣasa; Kumbha split that boulder with five well-aimed arrows.

sanskrit: saṃdhāya cānyaṃ sumukhaṃ śaram āśīviṣopamam ājaghāna mahātejā vakṣasi dvividāgrajam
english: Then nocking another fine-tipped arrow like a venomous serpent, the greatly resplendent one struck Dvivida's elder brother in the chest.

sanskrit: sa tu tena prahāreṇa maindo vānarayūthapaḥ marmaṇy abhihatas tena papāta bhuvi mūrchitaḥ
english: Mainda, the monkey troop-leader, struck in a vital spot by that blow, fell to the earth in a swoon.

sanskrit: aṅgado mātulau dṛṣṭvā patitau tau mahābalau abhidudrāva vegena kumbham udyatakārmukam
english: Aṅgada, seeing those two mighty maternal uncles fallen, charged swiftly at Kumbha with his bow raised.

sanskrit: tam āpatantaṃ vivyādha kumbhaḥ pañcabhir āyasaiḥ tribhiś cānyaiḥ śitair bāṇair mātaṃgam iva tomaraiḥ
english: As he came rushing, Kumbha pierced him with five iron arrows, and three other sharp arrows — as an elephant is pierced with darts.

sanskrit: so 'ṅgadaṃ vividhair bāṇaiḥ kumbho vivyādha vīryavān akuṇṭhadhārair niśitais tīkṣṇaiḥ kanakabhūṣaṇaiḥ
english: The valiant Kumbha pierced Aṅgada with various arrows, unblunted and sharp, keen and gold-adorned.

sanskrit: aṅgadaḥ pratividdhāṅgo vāliputro na kampate śilāpādapavarṣāṇi tasya mūrdhni vavarṣa ha
english: Aṅgada, the son of Vālin, though his body was pierced through, did not waver; he rained down upon Kumbha's head a shower of rocks and trees.

sanskrit: sa praciccheda tān sarvān bibheda ca punaḥ śilāḥ kumbhakarṇātmajaḥ śrīmān vāliputrasamīritān
english: The glorious son of Kumbhakarṇa cut down all of them and shattered again the rocks hurled by the son of Vālin.

sanskrit: āpatantaṃ ca saṃprekṣya kumbho vānarayūthapam bhruvor vivyādha bāṇābhyām ulkābhyām iva kuñjaram
english: And seeing the monkey troop-leader rushing at him, Kumbha pierced him between the eyebrows with two arrows, as if striking an elephant with two torches.

sanskrit: aṅgadaḥ pāṇinā netre pidhāya rudhirokṣite sālam āsannam ekena parijagrāha pāṇinā
english: Aṅgada, covering his eyes drenched with blood with one hand, seized with the other hand a nearby śāla tree.

sanskrit: tam indraketupratimaṃ vṛkṣaṃ mandarasaṃnibham samutsṛjantaṃ vegena paśyatāṃ sarvarakṣasām
english: That tree resembling Indra's banner post, like Mandara mountain — as he hurled it with force before the eyes of all the rākṣasas —

sanskrit: sa ciccheda śitair bāṇaiḥ saptabhiḥ kāyabhedanaiḥ aṅgado vivyathe 'bhīkṣṇaṃ sasāda ca mumoha ca
english: — Kumbha severed it with seven sharp arrows that pierce the body; Aṅgada was tormented again and again, sank down, and fell into a swoon.

sanskrit: aṅgadaṃ vyathitaṃ dṛṣṭvā sīdantam iva sāgare durāsadaṃ hariśreṣṭhā rāghavāya nyavedayan
english: Seeing Aṅgada tormented and sinking as if in an ocean, the foremost monkeys reported it to Rāghava — he was unapproachable.

sanskrit: rāmas tu vyathitaṃ śrutvā vāliputraṃ mahāhave vyādideśa hariśreṣṭhāñ jāmbavatpramukhāṃs tataḥ
english: Hearing that the son of Vālin was tormented in the great battle, Rāma then directed the foremost monkeys, headed by Jāmbavān.

sanskrit: te tu vānaraśārdūlāḥ śrutvā rāmasya śāsanam abhipetuḥ susaṃkruddhāḥ kumbham udyatakārmukam
english: Those tigers among monkeys, hearing Rāma's command, charged furiously at Kumbha with his bow raised.

sanskrit: tato drumaśilāhastāḥ kopasaṃraktalocanāḥ rirakṣiṣanto 'bhyapatann aṅgadaṃ vānararṣabhāḥ
english: Then the bulls among monkeys, with trees and stones in their hands, their eyes reddened with fury, rushed forward wishing to protect Aṅgada.

sanskrit: jāmbavāṃś ca suṣeṇaś ca vegadarśī ca vānaraḥ kumbhakarṇātmajaṃ vīraṃ kruddhāḥ samabhidudruvuḥ
english: Jāmbavān, Suṣeṇa, and the monkey Vegadarśī — all angry — ran together toward the heroic son of Kumbhakarṇa.

sanskrit: samīkṣyātatatas tāṃs tu vānarendrān mahābalān āvavāra śaraugheṇa nageneva jalāśayam
english: But seeing those greatly powerful lords of monkeys advancing, he blocked them with a flood of arrows as a mountain blocks a reservoir of water.

sanskrit: tasya bāṇacayaṃ prāpya na śoker ativartitum vānarendrā mahātmāno velām iva mahodadhiḥ
english: Meeting his mass of arrows, the great-souled monkey lords could not pass beyond, like the great ocean unable to pass beyond its shore.

sanskrit: tāṃs tu dṛṣṭvā harigaṇāñ śaravṛṣṭibhir arditān aṅgadaṃ pṛṣṭhataḥ kṛtvā bhrātṛjaṃ plavageśvaraḥ
english: Seeing those monkey troops afflicted by the rain of arrows, placing his nephew Aṅgada behind him, the lord of monkeys —

sanskrit: abhidudrāva vegena sugrīvaḥ kumbham āhave śailasānu caraṃ nāgaṃ vegavān iva kesarī
english: — Sugrīva charged swiftly at Kumbha in battle, like a swift-moving lion against an elephant roaming the mountain ridges.

sanskrit: utpāṭya ca mahāśailān aśvakarṇān dhavān bahūn anyāṃś ca vividhān vṛkṣāṃś cikṣepa ca mahābalaḥ
english: The mighty one uprooted great mountains, many aśvakarṇa and dhava trees, and various other trees, and hurled them.

sanskrit: tāṃ chādayantīm ākāśaṃ vṛkṣavṛṣṭiṃ durāsadām kumbhakarṇātmajaḥ śrīmāṃś ciccheda niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ
english: That unapproachable rain of trees that covered the sky, the glorious son of Kumbhakarṇa severed with his sharp arrows.

sanskrit: abhilakṣyeṇa tīvreṇa kumbhena niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ ācitās te drumā rejur yathā ghorāḥ śataghnayaḥ
english: Struck by Kumbha's sharp, unerring, fierce arrows, those trees shone like terrible śataghnī engines of war.

sanskrit: drumavarṣaṃ tu tac chinnaṃ dṛṣṭvā kumbhena vīryavān vānarādhipatiḥ śrīmān mahāsattvo na vivyathe
english: Seeing that rain of trees severed by the valiant Kumbha, the glorious lord of monkeys, of great essence, did not waver.

sanskrit: nirbhidyamānaḥ sahasā sahamānaś ca tāñ śarān kumbhasya dhanur ākṣipya babhañjendradhanuḥprabham
english: Suddenly pierced through and enduring those arrows, he snatched Kumbha's bow and broke it — that bow bright as Indra's rainbow.

sanskrit: avaplutya tataḥ śīghraṃ kṛtvā karma suduṣkaram abravīt kupitaḥ kumbhaṃ bhagnaśṛṅgam iva dvipam
english: Then leaping forward swiftly and having performed that most difficult deed, he angrily addressed Kumbha, who was like an elephant with a broken tusk:

sanskrit: nikumbhāgraja vīryaṃ te bāṇavegaṃ tad adbhutam saṃnatiś ca prabhāvaś ca tava vā rāvaṇasya vā
english: "O elder brother of Nikumbha, that valor of yours, that wonderful speed of your arrows, that skill and power — it is yours or Rāvaṇa's."

sanskrit: prahrādabalivṛtraghnakuberavaruṇopama ekas tvam anujāto 'si pitaraṃ balavattaraḥ
english: "O equal of Prahrāda, Bali, the slayer of Vṛtra, Kubera, and Varuṇa — you alone have been born surpassing your father in strength."

sanskrit: tvām evaikaṃ mahābāhuṃ śūlahastam ariṃdamam tridaśā nātivartante jitendriyam ivādhayaḥ
english: "You alone, O mighty-armed one, spear in hand, subduer of foes, the thirty gods cannot overcome, as diseases cannot overcome one who has conquered his senses."

sanskrit: varadānāt pitṛvyas te sahate devadānavān kumbhakarṇas tu vīryeṇa sahate ca surāsurān
english: "Your paternal uncle can endure gods and dānavas by virtue of boons received; but Kumbhakarṇa endured gods and asuras through sheer valor."

sanskrit: dhanuṣīndrajitas tulyaḥ pratāpe rāvaṇasya ca tvam adya rakṣasāṃ loke śreṣṭho 'si balavīryataḥ
english: "Equal to Indrajit with the bow, equal in glory to Rāvaṇa — today you are the foremost in the world of rākṣasas in strength and valor."

sanskrit: mahāvimardaṃ samare mayā saha tavādbhutam adya bhūtāni paśyantu śakraśambarayor iva
english: "Let the beings of the world witness today this wonderful great clash between you and me in battle, as they once witnessed that between Indra and Śambara."

sanskrit: kṛtam apratimaṃ karma darśitaṃ cāstrakauśalam pātitā harivīrāś ca tvayaite bhīmavikramāḥ
english: "An incomparable feat has been accomplished, skill with weapons has been displayed, and these monkey heroes of terrible prowess have been felled by you."

sanskrit: upālambhabhayāc cāpi nāsi vīra mayā hataḥ kṛtakarmā pariśrānto viśrāntaḥ paśya me balam
english: "Nor have I slain you yet for fear of censure, O hero — you have done your work and are weary; rest, and then witness my strength."

sanskrit: tena sugrīvavākyena sāvamānena mānitaḥ agner ājyahutasyeva tejas tasyābhyavardhata
english: Honored — though with contempt — by those words of Sugrīva, his energy grew like the flame of a fire fed with clarified butter.

sanskrit: tataḥ kumbhaḥ samutpatya sugrīvam abhipadya ca ājaghānorasi kruddho vajravegena muṣṭinā
english: Then Kumbha leaped up, fell upon Sugrīva, and furiously struck him on the chest with a fist of thunderbolt force.

sanskrit: tasya carma ca pusphoṭa saṃjajñe cāsya śoṇitam sa ca muṣṭir mahāvegaḥ pratijaghne 'sthimaṇḍale
english: The skin of Sugrīva's chest burst open and blood appeared; and that fist of great momentum rebounded from his firm circle of bones.

sanskrit: tadā vegena tatrāsīt tejaḥ prajvālitaṃ muhuḥ vajraniṣpeṣasaṃjātajvālā merau yathā girau
english: Then from that force a flame was kindled there again and again — like the flames born from the crushing of a thunderbolt on Mount Meru.

sanskrit: sa tatrābhihatas tena sugrīvo vānararṣabhaḥ muṣṭiṃ saṃvartayām āsa vajrakalpaṃ mahābalaḥ
english: Struck there by him, Sugrīva, the bull among monkeys, the mighty one, gathered his fist into a thunderbolt-like shape.

sanskrit: arciḥsahasravikacaṃ ravimaṇḍalasaprabham sa muṣṭiṃ pātayām āsa kumbhasyorasi vīryavān
english: Blazing with a thousand flames, bright as the solar orb, the valiant one drove that fist down onto Kumbha's chest.

sanskrit: muṣṭinābhihatas tena nipapātāśu rākṣasaḥ lohitāṅga ivākāśād dīptaraśmir yadṛcchayā
english: Struck by that fist, the rākṣasa fell at once, like the planet Mars with its blazing rays falling from the sky by chance.

sanskrit: kumbhasya patato rūpaṃ bhagnasyorasi muṣṭinā babhau rudrābhipannasya yathārūpaṃ gavāṃ pateḥ
english: The appearance of Kumbha as he fell, his chest shattered by the fist, resembled the form of the lord of cattle assailed by Rudra.

sanskrit: tasmin hate bhīmaparākrameṇa plavaṃgamānām ṛṣabheṇa yuddhe mahī saśailā savanā cacāla bhayaṃ ca rakṣāṃsy adhikaṃ viveśa
english: When he was slain by the bull among leapers, of terrible valor, in battle, the earth with its mountains and forests trembled, and a great fear entered the rākṣasas.
